verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              स्वाध्याये कृतयत्नस्य नरस्य च पितामह । धर्मकामस्य धर्मात्मन् किं नु श्रेय इहोच्यते ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said “Having spoken in this way, the twice-born Rishi of austere penances, viz., Shuka, lived on his success, renouncing the four sorts of faults.

verses.sanskrit: बहुधा दर्शने लोके श्रेयो यदिह मन्यसे । अस्मिँल्लोके परे चैव तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥२॥
verses.english: Renouncing also the eight kinds of Tamas, he dismissed the five kinds of Rajas. Gifted with great intelligence, he the renounced the attribute of Sattva. All this seemed extremely wonderful.

verses.sanskrit: महानयं धर्मपथो बहुशाखश्च भारत । किंस्विदेवेह धर्माणामनुष्ठेयतमं मतम् ॥३॥
verses.english: He then lived in that eternal station which is shorn of attributes, freed from every indication, that is, in Brahma, shining like a smokeless fire.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मस्यो महतो राजन् बहुशाखस्य तत्त्वतः । यन्मूलं परमं तात तत्सर्वं ब्रूह्यशेषतः ॥४॥
verses.english: Meteors began to shoot. The points of the horizon seemed to be ablaze. The Earth trembled. All these phenomena seemed extremely wonderful.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              हन्त ते कथयिष्यामि येन श्रेयो ह्यवाप्स्यसि । पीत्वाऽमृतमिव प्राज्ञो ज्ञानतृप्तो भविष्यसि ॥५॥
verses.english: The trees began to throw off their branches and the mountains their summits. Loud peals were heard that seemed to rive the Himavat mountains.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मस्य विधयो नैके ये वै प्रोक्ता महर्षिभिः । स्वं स्वं विज्ञानमाश्रित्य दमस्तेषां परायणम् ॥६॥
verses.english: The Sun seemed at that moment to be shorn of effulgence. Fire refused to burn forth. The lakes and rivers and seas were all moved.

verses.sanskrit: दमं निःश्रेयसं प्राहुर्वृद्धा निश्चितदर्शिनः । ब्राह्मणस्य विशेषेण दमो धर्मः सनातनः ॥७॥
verses.english: Vasava poured showers of rain of excellent taste and smell. A pure breeze began to blow, carrying excellent taste and smell. A pure breeze began to blow, carrying excellent perfumes.

verses.sanskrit: दमात्तस्य क्रियासिद्धिर्यथावदुपलभ्यते । दमो दानं तथा यज्ञानधीतं चातिवर्तते ॥८॥
verses.english: Shuka, as he went through the sky, saw two beautiful summits, one belonging to Himavat and another to Meru. These were side by side with each other. One of them was made of gold and was, therefore, yellow; the other was white, being made of silver.

verses.sanskrit: दमस्तेजो वर्धयति पवित्रं च दमः परम् । विपाप्मा तेजसा युक्तः पुरुषो विन्दते महत् ॥९॥
verses.english: Each of them, O Bharata, was a hundred Yojanas in height and of the same breath. Indeed, as Shuka went towards the north, he beheld those two beautiful summits,

verses.sanskrit: दमेन सदृशं धर्मं नान्यं लोकेषु शुश्रुम । दमो हि परमो लोके प्रशस्तः सर्वधर्मिणाम् ॥१०॥
verses.english: With a fearless heart he dashed against those two summits that were close to each other. Unable to bear the force, the summits were suddenly rent in two parts.

verses.sanskrit: प्रेत्य चात्र मनुष्येन्द्र परमं विन्दते सुखम् । दमेन हि समायुक्तो महान्तं धर्ममश्नुते ॥११॥
verses.english: The spectacle, O monarch, was extremely wonderful to look at. Shuka pierced through those summits, for they were unable to stop his onward course. At this a loud noise was made in heaven by the dwellers thereof.

verses.sanskrit: सुखं दान्तः प्रस्वपिति सुखं च प्रतिबुध्यते । सुखं पर्येति लोकांश्च मनश्चास्य प्रसीदति ॥१२॥
verses.english: The Gandharvas and the Rishis also and others who lived in that mountain sent up loud cheers at the sight of the mountain being rent in two and Shuka passing through it. Indeed, O Bharata, a loud noise was heard everywhere at that moment, saying,-Excellent, Excellent.

verses.sanskrit: अदान्तः पुरुषः क्लेशमभीक्ष्णं प्रतिपद्यते । अनर्थांश्च बहूनन्यान् प्रसृजत्यात्मदोषजान् ॥१३॥
verses.english: He was worshipped by the Gandharvas and the Rishis, by Yakhas and Rakshasas, and by all tribes of the Vidyadharas.

verses.sanskrit: आश्रमेषु चतुर्ष्बाहुर्दममेवोत्तमं व्रतम् । तस्य लिङ्गानि वक्ष्यामि येषां समुदयो दमः ॥१४॥
verses.english: The entire sky became covered with celestial flowers showered from heaven at that moment when Shuka thus cut through that impenetrable barrier, O king.

verses.sanskrit: क्षमा धृतिरहिंसा च समता सत्यमार्जवम् । इन्द्रियाभिजयो दाक्ष्यं मार्दवं ह्रीरचापलम् ॥१५॥
verses.english: The pious Shuka then saw from a high region the extremely beautiful celestial river Mandakini, running below through a region adorned by many flowering groves and forests.

verses.sanskrit: अकार्पण्यमसंरम्भः संतोषः प्रियवादिता । अविहिंसानसूया चाप्येषां समुदयो दमः ॥१६॥
गुरुपूजा च कौरव्य दया भूतेषु पैशुनम् । जनवादं मृषावादं स्तुतिनिन्दाविसर्जनम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: In these waters many beautiful Apsaras were playing. Seeing Shuka who was bodiless, those naked aerial beings felt no shame.

verses.sanskrit: कामं क्रोधं च लोभं च दर्पं स्तम्भं विकत्थनम् । रोषमीर्ष्या॑वमानं च नैव दान्तो निषेवते ॥१८॥
अनिन्दितो ह्यकामात्मा नाल्पेष्वर्थ्यनसूयकः । समुद्रकल्पः स नरो न कथंचन पूर्यते ॥१९॥
verses.english: Learning that Shuka had undertaken his great journey, his father Vyasa, filled with affection, followed him behind along the same aerial path.

verses.sanskrit: अहं त्वयि ममत्वं च मयि तेषु तथाऽप्यहम् । पूर्वसम्बन्धिसंयोगं नैतद्दान्तो निषेवते ॥२०॥
verses.english: Meanwhile Shuka, passing through thai region of the sky which is above the region of the wind, showed his Yoga-power and identified himself with Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वा ग्राम्यास्तथाऽऽरण्या याश्च लोके प्रवृत्तयः । निन्दां चैव प्रशंसां च यो नाश्रयति मुच्यते ॥२१॥
verses.english: Following the subtile path of high Yoga, Vyasa of austere penances, reached within the twinkling of the eye that place whence Shuka first started.

verses.sanskrit: मैत्रोऽथ शीलसम्पन्नः प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मविच्च यः । मुक्तस्य विविधैः सङ्गैस्तस्य प्रेत्य फलं महत् ॥२२॥
verses.english: Proceeding along the same way, Vyasa saw the mountain summit rent in two parts and through which Shuka has passed. Meeting the Island-born ascetic, the Rishis began to describe to him the achievements of his own.

verses.sanskrit: सुवृत्तः शीलसम्पन्नः प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मविद्बुधः । प्राप्येह लोके सत्कारं सुगतिं प्रतिपद्यते ॥२३॥
verses.english: Vyasa, however, began to lament, loudly naming his son and causing the three worlds to resound with the noise he made.

verses.sanskrit: कर्म यच्छुभमेवेह सद्भिराचरितं च यत् । तदेव ज्ञानयुक्तस्य मुनेर्वर्त्म न हीयते ॥२४॥
verses.english: Meanwhile, the pious Shuka, who had entered all things, had become the soul of all things, and had acquired omnipresence, answered his fathers by uttering the monosyllable BHO in the form of an echo.

verses.sanskrit: निष्क्रम्य वनमास्थाय ज्ञानयुक्तो जितेन्द्रियः । कालाकाङ्क्षी चरत्येवं ब्रह्मभूयाय कल्पते ॥२५॥
verses.english: Thereat, the entire universe of mobile and immobile creatures, uttering the monosyllable BHO, echoed the answer of Shuka.

verses.sanskrit: अभयं यस्य भूतेभ्यो भूतानामभयं यतः । तस्य देहाद्विमुक्तस्य भयं नास्ति कुतश्चन ॥२६॥
verses.english: Thereforward, when sounds are made in mountain-caves or on mountain-breasts, the latter, as if in answer to Shuka, still echo them.

verses.sanskrit: अवाचिनोति कर्माणि न च सम्प्रचिनोति ह । समः सर्वेषु भूतेषु मैत्रायणगतिश्चरेत् ॥२७॥
verses.english: Having renounced all the attributes of sound, etc., and showing his Yoga-power in the manner of his disappearance, Shuka in this way acquired the highest station.

verses.sanskrit: शकुनीनामिवाकाशे जले वारिचरस्य च । यथा गतिर्न दृश्येत तथा तस्य न संशयः ॥२८॥
verses.english: Seeing that glory and power of his son of immeasurable energy, Vyasa sat down on the breast of the mountain and began to think of his son sorrowfully.

verses.sanskrit: गृहानुत्सृज्य यो राजन् मोक्षमेवाभिपद्यते । लोकास्तेजोमयास्तस्य कल्पन्ते शाश्वतीः समाः ॥२९॥
verses.english: Seeing the Rishi seated there, the Apsaras who were sporting on the banks of the celestial river Mandakini, became all moved with shame and dispirited.

verses.sanskrit: संन्यस्य सर्वकर्माणि संन्यस्य विधिवत्तपः । संन्यस्य विविधा विद्याः सर्वं संन्यस्य चैव ह ॥३०॥
verses.english: Some of them, to hide their nakedness, plunged into the river, and some entered the groves hard by, and some quickly took up their clothes, at seeing the Rishi.

verses.sanskrit: कामे शुचिरनावृत्तः प्रसन्नात्माऽऽत्मविच्छुचिः । प्राप्येह लोके सत्कारं स्वर्ग समभिपद्यते ॥३१॥
यच्च पैतामहं स्थानं ब्रह्मराशिसमुद्भवम् । गुहायां पिहितं नित्यं तद्दमेनाभिगम्यते ॥३२॥
ज्ञानारामस्य बुद्धस्य सर्वभूताविरोधिनः । नावृत्तिभयमस्तीह परलोकभयं कुतः ॥३३॥
एक एव दमे दोषो द्वितीयो नोपपद्यते । यदेनं क्षमया युक्तमशक्तं मन्यते जनः ॥३४॥
एकोऽस्य सुमहाप्राज्ञः दोषः स्यात् सुमहान्गुणः । क्षमया विपुला लोकाः सुलभा हि सहिष्णुता ॥३५॥
दान्तस्य किमरण्येन तथाऽदान्तस्य भारत । यत्रैव निवसेद्दान्तस्तदरण्यं स चाश्रमः ॥३६॥

वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              एतद्भीष्मस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा युधिष्ठिरः । अमृतेनेव संतृप्तः प्रहृष्टः समपद्यत ॥३७॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said Having said these words, Bhishma, with mind fixed upon Krishna, said,-'Salutations to Krishna.' And bowed to him.

verses.sanskrit: पुनश्च परिपप्रच्छ भीष्मं धर्मभृतां वरम् । तपः प्रीतः स चोवाच तस्मै सर्वं कुरूद्वह ॥३८॥
